event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_after_the_fal: Your voice disappears in the shouting; the child thinks people are mocking them and tries to leave.
You calm the onlookers too; the child stays still without feeling humiliated.
The child listens for a second, then tries to prove they are fine by standing.
You give them something simple to answer and they stay seated.
Keep them seated by talking
You clear air and space, but the child is already trying to put one foot under them.
Push the onlookers back
You mistake the silence for courage; the child stands and staggers toward the steps.
You immediately spot the worrying signs and clear space around the child.
You see something is wrong, but too late to stop the first step.
You notice the unfocused stare and keep them from standing too quickly.
Watch their eyes and answers
A child falls hard from a low wall during play. They do not cry, barely answer, and already try to stand while the others crowd around.
After the Fall
The adult understands what happened and takes over without making the child walk.
Describe the fall exactly
The adult takes longer to understand and the child feels forced to keep pretending to be fine.
Say it is nothing
The child finally accepts staying put while the adult comes closer.
Help them sit without carrying them
The child takes one step and their knee folds. An adult finally reaches the lane, but only sees a circle of children and does not yet understand the fall.
The Second Step
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_boiling_pot.c: You let go immediately from the heat; some water splashes the floor and everyone makes you step back.
The tray supports the handle and frees the cord without spilling the water.
Slide a tray under the handle
The cloth pulls taut against the floor before it can drag the pot farther.
Step on the loose apron tail
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_boiling_pot.t: A pot of boiling water sits too close to the edge of a low table. An apron cord has caught its handle; the person wearing it is already walking toward the door.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_breakfall_les: The instructor repeats the move slowly and shows exactly where the arm must not lock.
You lock your arm at the wrong moment and the impact knocks the breath out of you in front of the group.
You turn the push into a clean roll and keep enough balance to demonstrate the finish.
You roll too late and end in the sand, unhurt but with the technique still wrong.
You spread the impact and get up without planting a hand into the ground.
You anticipate the wrong side and fall stiffly under two students’ laughter.
You spot the motion before contact and adjust your feet without breaking the drill.
You see the push but not its exact angle; the fall stays messy.
You read the angle and choose the right side to absorb the fall.
Read the shoulder before the push
An instructor drills falls on packed sand. After two demonstrations it is your turn: a partner will push you sideways, and locking an arm is exactly the mistake to avoid.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid.cho: The wheel escapes you and the cart pivots, exposing its open side to the thieves.
You wedge the wheel against a post and turn the cart into stable cover.
You slow the cart, but a sack is already sliding off the bed.
You stop the wheel and keep the cart from becoming a danger itself.
You choose the wrong lane; the thief reaches the corner and a second sack vanishes.
You read the detour and reach the corner first; the sack stays behind without a fight.
You force a turn, but the thief keeps the sack and reaches the crates.
You close the lane and the thief has to drop the sack to get through.
The drawbar drops to the ground and makes it impossible to haul the whole cart away quickly.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid.tex: Three petty bandits rush a stopped cart and yank its cover. The driver drops to one knee; a wheel starts rolling and one thief is already tearing away a sack.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid_i01: The stack tips the other way and leaves the driver safe.
Kick the bottom crate toward the wall
The thief gains ground, but nobody chases under falling boxes.
Let the sack go and secure the cart
The driver clears the line before the boxes fall.
Pull the driver behind the wheel
The first sack drops or vanishes behind stacked crates. A bandit shoves the stack to cover the escape; the top boxes start tipping toward the driver.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_cart_raid_i02: You gain a few meters then have to stop; the driver blames you for abandoning the cart.
The bandit backs away and runs. Some cargo is missing, but the blade leaves with him.
Give the bandit a clear exit
You recover what is within reach without turning the theft into a duel.
Keep distance and recover the dropped sack
Two bandits run. The last stays by the drawbar, winded, with a small blade drawn mostly to scare; behind you, the driver wants the sack back.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump.ch: Your foot slips at the edge; you drop into the mud and the bank crumbles behind you.
You clear the ditch cleanly and reveal a line that avoids the crumbling bank.
You reach the far side on your knees, but a whole clump slides into the ditch and shrinks the foothold.
You clear the ditch and immediately spot the takeoff point that still holds.
The plank pivots under your weight and drops sideways, taking stones into the water.
You find two solid supports and turn the plank into a proper little bridge.
Your bridge holds for a second, then sinks on one side; the crossing gets narrower.
You wedge the plank between two roots and make a precarious but usable crossing.
You knock loose clumps away with a stick and keep to the firmest crossing.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump.te: Rain has swollen a ditch across the path. One bank is already crumbling underfoot, and the detour would bring everyone back after the crossing closes.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_ditch_jump_i0: The stone pins the wood just enough to offer a foothold.
Pin the plank with a stone
The bundle lands in the dirt, but both hands are free for the crossing.
Throw the bundle across to free both hands
You point out exactly where to step; no one tests the soft bank blindly.
Point out the only solid foothold
A slab of earth slides into the water. One narrow foothold remains and the plank tilts on the other side; someone is still stranded across.
The last foot clears. The plank then drops into the water, unusable.
Nobody falls, but the group gives up the shortcut and loses time.
You save the plank, but the final crossing becomes clumsy and embarrassing.
Try to save the plank too
The last child is straddling the plank when a root cracks. One action will decide whether the group leaves together or abandons the crossing.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_doorway_evacu: Nobody runs under the beam while you work out an exit.
Seat the younger children along the wall
You clear the only exit that does not pass under the beam.
Dump the baskets away from the hatch
The hook holds the shelf at a distance and opens a narrow lane.
Catch the shelf with a long hook
In a neighborhood shed, a cracked beam knocks a shelf across the main door. Three younger children are still inside; a small rear hatch exists, but its route is cluttered.
The Closing Threshold
Each child crosses with one hand held before releasing the previous one.
Make a hand line to the yard
Yard light comes in and the first child agrees to crawl through.
Wedge the hatch fully open
A rough lane appears through the slippery floor.
Sweep the shavings with a lid
The hatch opens, but the first child freezes at the dark opening. Beyond it, a sack of shavings has spilled and made the floor slippery to the yard.
The Rear Hatch
Everyone exits through the route that was already made safe.
Finish through the hatch despite the shortcut
Nobody mistakes the opening for a safe exit.
Block the new gap with a basket
The last child hesitates between two instructions and comes out crying, unhurt but embarrassed.
Switch exits at the last moment
The last child reaches the hatch when a sharp crack comes from the main door. The beam shifts and the shelf suddenly opens a tempting gap toward the main exit.
The Beam Moves Again
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_falling_crate: The stack collapses early, before the group enters its path.
Knock down the two bottom crates on purpose
The stack stops pressing against the wheel and falls in one predictable direction.
Pull the wheelbarrow away from the base
You focus on the wrong thing; the whole stack falls into the lane and the others drive you out of the area.
Try to save the top crate
A stack of empty crates leans after a wheelbarrow hits its base. The crates are light but tall; a small group is walking behind it without looking up.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_falling_frame: The post slips from you and the frame falls sideways, trapping someone under the canvas.
You guide the fall all the way down and keep the post away from heads.
You slow the fall without stopping it; the frame collapses across the lane.
You turn the frame toward open space and avoid a direct hit.
Catch the side post
Your shouts mix with the crowd; one person moves the wrong way under the canvas.
The crowd opens a clean circle; the frame drops into empty space.
Most people step back, but someone remains hidden behind the stretched canvas.
You get everyone out of the line before the frame hits the ground.
Clear everyone from beneath it
The canvas loses its grip on the wind and the frame comes down less violently.
Tear the canvas along its seam
A large decorated canvas frame tilts after one foot snaps. Wind pushes it toward the street; several people pass underneath without seeing the descending post.
The Frame Above the Street
Light gets in and the person sees a clear way out.
Lift only the corner with no wood
The person gets out, but a post rolls loose and breaks a nearby decoration.
Rip the whole canvas away
The person follows your voice and gets out without crawling across broken posts.
Guide their hand toward the clear edge
The frame is down, but the canvas has folded over someone and hides the broken posts. They move underneath without knowing which way is clear.
Under the Canvas
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_frayed_swing_: The rope holds once more, then snaps on the empty return. The others blame you for waiting for that sound.
The game stops before the rope carries one more load.
Stop the next launch by holding the board
Without a seat, nobody can restart the swing before checking the rope.
A makeshift swing creaks over hard ground. With each pass, more white fibers show at the upper knot; the next child is already sitting on the board.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_kitchen_greas: The stool catches the cloth; the oily fabric falls burning to the floor.
You clear stool and basket in one move, leaving almost bare floor around the pan.
You pull the stool away, but the cloth still slides near the flame.
You clear the route and move the nearest fuel away.
Pull the stool clear
The salt smothers part of the oil on the floor, but a cloth is already blackening.
Dump the salt bin onto the spill
You use the wrong lid; it slips and a tongue of flame catches the nearby cloth.
You set the lid without moving the pan and push everyone back from the fire.
You cover most of the pan, but one edge stays open and the flame finds air.
You cut the pan off from air before the oil can spread.
Smother the pan under a lid
A pan of oil ignites in a shared kitchen. Flame is already licking a hanging cloth; two people are outside and someone is still in the small back room.
The Oil Catches Fire
The tile pushes the cloth away from the threshold without bringing hands close.
Push it with a tile
You bypass the threshold and reach the other side of the room.
Use the small side window
The blanket pins the cloth and opens a low path.
Slide a wet blanket over it
The burning cloth falls from its hook near the threshold. The main exit stays open, but the fabric cuts the shortest path to the back room.
The Oily Cloth
The panel gives way and lets air through, but broken wood stays on the floor.
Break the light lower panel
The person finds the handle and finally opens the right way.
Call out where the handle is
You stay under the smoke and free the door from outside.
Crawl to the door and open it
A voice answers behind the back-room door: smoke hides the handle and the person is pushing the wrong way. Heat is building at the ceiling.
Someone in the Back Room
The mat keeps smoking and an adult has to run back. Your haste is obvious.
Say the fire is over
The mat ends up in the yard where the embers can be soaked without trapping smoke.
Roll the mat outside
Water cuts off the embers’ spread before reaching the center.
Wet the edges first
Everyone is outside when the smell of burning returns. Under a mat near the threshold, a few red embers are still creeping through the fibers.
Embers Under the Mat
The ladder forces you backward; it misses the window but you end on the floor covered in sawdust.
The shutter takes the first contact and the person behind moves away from the impact.
The wedge stops the slide before the top reaches the window.
Kick a wedge under the foot
A long ladder against a wall starts sliding when its foot hits sawdust. Nobody is on it, but its top is dropping toward an open window where someone works with their back turned.
The baskets close the lane without trapping the animal; the dog slows enough for the situation to change.
Make a screen with two empty baskets
You slip in front of it; the dog bounds over you and its rope lashes your ankle.
You keep exactly the right distance and guide its run toward an open yard.
You divert the dog, but it immediately switches toward a more crowded stall.
You open an empty line and draw it away from the passers-by.
You think the rope is clear; it wraps a table leg and throws baskets into the lane.
You see where the rope will go taut and clear that space before impact.
You spot the rope too late to catch it; it keeps sweeping the lane.
You anticipate the rope’s next bounce and create a safe opening.
A panicked dog bolts from a yard with a long rope on its collar. It barrels through baskets; a small child freezes directly in its path.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_panicked_dog_: The gate forces the dog to turn before the collision.
Push a gate between them
The noise stops; the dog slows, but keeps moving toward the end.
Throw a cloth over the rattling baskets
The passers-by press to the wall and clear the alley.
Shout “left!” to the passers-by
The child is clear, but a shutter bangs and startles the dog again. It veers into an alley where two people approach without seeing it.
It Changes Target
The dog sniffs the bowl; the tension drops enough to wait.
Slide a bowl of water forward
Seeing an exit, the dog stops pressing into the wall.
Leave it one exit toward the yard
You pin the rope without entering biting range.
Pin the rope away from its mouth
The dog ends up under a stair, back to the wall, ears flat. Its rope is finally reachable, but it growls whenever a hand approaches.
Cornered Under the Stairs
The rope changes hands without anyone crawling under the stairs.
Slide the rope to her along the ground
She gets the dog back, but the sudden grab triggers one last bark and a sharp scare.
Let her grab the collar
She slows down and calls the dog instead of grabbing it. The rope finally returns to her hand.
Gently stop her hand
A neighbor runs up and recognizes the collar. She reaches too quickly; the dog tenses again, and everything you gained could vanish in a second.
The Recognized Collar
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_playfight_red: The others start shouting again and the pinned child mostly remembers that you chose the show.
Cheer for the fight to continue
You refuse to count the rest as play; the child on top finally gets up.
The familiar word interrupts the momentum and everyone recognizes the rule was crossed.
A playfight turns wrong when one child keeps going after the agreed signal. The other is no longer laughing and is pinned under a knee; nobody knows if the game is still on.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_runaway_handc: Someone misunderstands and crosses in front of the cart; every other option has to be abandoned to avoid them.
Your call opens a route toward an incline where the cart loses speed on its own.
The street clears late; the cart hurts no one but crushes goods on the ground.
People move aside and the cart ends its run in empty sacks.
Open the lane ahead of it
The crates break under the wheel and absorb enough speed to keep it away from people.
Drop two empty crates in front of the wheel
The handle yanks you off-line; the cart hits a stall before stopping.
You guide the wheel into the gutter and stop the cart in an empty angle.
You turn the cart, but it scrapes a wall and knocks over a stack of baskets.
You force the handle toward a post and the cart jams there without hitting anyone.
Grab the handle and turn it
A loaded handcart rolls alone down a sloping street after its chock breaks. Its handle whips side to side; farther down, pedestrians have not seen it yet.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storeroom_int: The bell fills the street while you keep a door between yourself and the intruder.
Ring, then block the outside door
A board cracks under your foot. The figure turns and you lose the advantage of the doorway.
You work out where the intruder can flee and warn people without entering the storeroom.
After closing time, wood scrapes in a nearby storeroom. The door is ajar and a figure is searching sacks; beside you, a pull-cord bell rings directly into the street.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storm_banner_: You miss the cloth and the bar swings lower, directly over the lane.
You step on the trailing cloth at the right moment and the banner nearly stops billowing.
You pin one corner of cloth, but the other rope still whips and the bar keeps turning.
You pin enough cloth to reduce the wind load.
Run onto the trailing cloth
Two calls conflict and people cross paths under the bar.
Your call travels mouth to mouth and the whole lane clears before the next gust.
The crowd moves, but leaves one group trapped near the pole.
You open an empty corridor exactly under the bar’s path.
Clear the crowd in sections
The cloth loses one tension point; the bar stays suspended but spins more slowly.
Undo the lower cloth tie
A festival banner tears in a gust. Its long wooden bar still hangs by two ropes above a crowded lane; one attachment starts slipping.
The Banner Tears Its Bar Loose
He crawls out of the danger zone while the bar keeps descending.
Send the merchant under the cart handle
The rope takes the load again for a few seconds.
Lift the rope back onto the pole
The cart turns and frees just enough room for the merchant.
Swing the cart by its handle
One rope slips its ring and lashes the pole. The bar drops on one side; a merchant is trapped behind his cart directly under the low end.
The Rope Whips
You use the cloth like a leash and lay the bar against the wall.
Guide the end with the cloth
The bar hits the stones without striking anyone. The festival lost a banner, not a passer-by.
Let it fall into the cleared space
You save part of the cloth, but the bar scrapes a stall and the merchant drives you away.
Hold the banner to save it
The last tie tears. One end of the bar drops toward the cleared ground while the other stays caught in the cloth like a lever.
The Bar Drops
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_storm_shutter: A gust tears you from the wall; the shutter swings again and nearly rips out its lower hinge.
You pin the shutter in the wind shadow and buy several clear seconds.
You slow the shutter without securing it; the screws keep pulling from the wood.
You hold the shutter long enough for a rope to be passed around it.
Pin the shutter to the wall
You turn the post into an anchor point; the tearing hinge still has to be dealt with.
Loop the rope around the post
You misread the rhythm; the next gust hits while everyone is moving in.
You spot a real lull and clear the passers-by before anyone touches the shutter.
The lull is shorter than expected; the hinge takes the load again before the rope is set.
You call the right lull and everyone acts during two calm seconds.
Wait for the gap between gusts
A squall hits the street. The upper hinge of a large shutter pulls from the wall; the panel slams above the lane and its closing bar starts coming loose.
The Shutter Becomes a Weight
The bar comes free into your hands; the panel stays heavy but less dangerous.
Grab the bar before it falls
Nobody stays under the shutter, but the wood keeps pulling on the rope.
Clear the whole lane
The rope turns the fall into a controlled lowering.
Lower it under tension
The upper hinge tears free completely. The shutter now hangs from the lower hinge and the rope while its metal bar slides toward the edge.
The Hinge Tears Free
The bar stops against the stone and the lane becomes safe again.
Trap the bar against the gutter
You stop it, but the impact in your fingers leaves you shaking and embarrassed.
Grab it directly
People move aside and the bar ends its run against a wall.
Open a lane in front of it
The shutter finally reaches the ground, but the closing bar rolls downhill toward people’s ankles. The danger changed shape; it did not disappear.
The Bar in the Street
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_too_many_to_f: All three turn toward you. You have to run and the vendor loses the time you meant to buy.
You keep the useful route in mind without giving the three adults another target.
Mark the courtyard and turn back
The warning goes around the street without your group entering the lane.
Pass a warning through a nearby window
Three adults with clubs search a small vendor’s bags and block the street. They have not noticed your group yet; behind them, a courtyard connects to another lane.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash.ch: The workbench creates a physical barrier without touching the tool.
Your words sound like a challenge; the tool strikes the wall to shut you up.
The room goes quiet; they lower the tool before anyone else moves.
The person hesitates but does not lower the tool yet.
Their gaze leaves the other apprentice and drops to the tool in their own hand.
Make them look at what they are threatening
You choose the wrong side; the tool flashes past you and hits the wall.
You read the move before it starts and pull the other apprentice out of reach.
You avoid the first swing, but the person keeps the tool between you.
You see the hand is shaking more than aiming and stay outside the line.
Read the grip before moving in
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash.te: Two older apprentices argue in a workshop. One grabs a heavy chisel and raises it; the other is trapped between bench and wall, too close to step back.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_tool_flash_i0: The bench breaks their line and keeps them apart.
Block the counterattack with the bench
The sharp command freezes the scene; the tool lowers without yet being dropped.
The trapped apprentice finally sees an exit that does not pass the other person.
The chisel hits wall or bench instead of a person. The impact shocks everyone; the armed hand stays tight, but the other apprentice now wants to lunge.
You separate actions from insults; the adult can act without guessing the rest.
Report only the actions you saw
The tension turns into anger at you; you leave the workshop under insults.
You protect the one who was cornered, but the other mostly remembers your accusation.
The chisel ends up on the floor. An adult runs in and immediately asks who started it while both apprentices talk at once and look for a witness.
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_younger_first: Your brace skids out; the plank drops farther and {{npc_childhood_younger}} loses faith in your plan.
You lock the broken hinge and restore enough footing for them to take part in the rescue.
The brace slows the movement without stopping it; you still have to decide how to get them up.
You wedge the wood against a post; the platform finally stops moving.
Brace the plank before pulling
You grab too late; both arms slam the plank and {{npc_childhood_younger}} snaps that you nearly made them let go.
You absorb the fall and bring them back against the platform without panic.
You stop the fall, but {{npc_childhood_younger}} stays hanging and shouts not to yank blindly.
You stop the fall without twisting their arm; {{npc_childhood_younger}} finds a foothold.
Catch their wrist
You keep your voice low and {{npc_childhood_younger}} finds the crossbar underfoot alone.
Guide their foot toward a hold
A younger child shouts their name while running across an old platform. A plank snaps; {{npc_childhood_younger}} is left hanging by both hands above a stack of crates.
“I’m {{npc_childhood_younger}}!”
On three, you push and pull together; {{npc_childhood_younger}} climbs with the rhythm.
Count the moves together
You haul them up quickly, but {{npc_childhood_younger}} immediately pulls away, upset at being given no part in it.
Haul them up anyway
{{npc_childhood_younger}} plants a foot exactly where you point and climbs one step.
Point to the crossbar
{{npc_childhood_younger}} finds one foothold, then pushes your free hand away. “Not like a sack. Tell me where the other foot goes.” The plank keeps creaking.
Not Like a Sack
You refuse to turn it into a lesson. {{npc_childhood_younger}} nods, unconvinced.
Say it was just luck
You promise to show them how to test a foothold before climbing.
Promise a real lesson
You agree to teach, provided they warn you before rushing in.
Set one rule: ask before danger
Standing on the crates, {{npc_childhood_younger}} looks at the broken plank, then at your hands. “Next time, teach me before pulling me out.”
“Teach Me Instead”
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_younger_lt_s0: You put the planks away. {{npc_childhood_younger}} does not argue for long, but keeps looking at the wall.
Stop the lesson at the first creak
You watch without correcting the first move. {{npc_childhood_younger}} changes the order on their own after feeling one plank pivot.
Let them choose the order
You make them shake each plank before putting weight on it. {{npc_childhood_younger}} repeats the test until finding the loose one alone.
Teach them to test every foothold
A year later, {{npc_childhood_younger}} finds you by a low wall and lays three planks like steps. “This time, show me without lifting me.” They wait for your first instruction.
“Show Me Without Touching”
The question is enough. {{npc_childhood_younger}} tests each piece and finds the rope without you naming it.
Ask “what is moving?”
The route becomes safe, but {{npc_childhood_younger}} reminds you that the lesson was supposed to belong to them.
Retie the rope yourself
You point out the problem and {{npc_childhood_younger}} chooses to retie the knot before continuing.
Point out the rope, not the solution
{{npc_childhood_younger}} has built a small route between two crates and refuses to be held. A badly tensioned rope shifts in the middle; they only ask whether you see anything wrong.
The First Lesson That Counts
You study the marks before answering. {{npc_childhood_younger}} relaxes when you take the work seriously.
Acknowledge they found a method
You limit your help to what was asked. {{npc_childhood_younger}} keeps control of the rest of the course.
Offer to check only the last knot
You take the planks down. {{npc_childhood_younger}} watches without helping and asks you for nothing else that day.
Take down the course as too dangerous
{{npc_childhood_younger}} waits beside a course built from crates. “You wouldn’t show me, so I asked someone else.” One plank bears three charcoal test marks.
The Course Without You
You remove the risk immediately. Once down, {{npc_childhood_younger}} pushes you away: “I was coming down.”
Grab them before they ask
You give information, not an order. {{npc_childhood_younger}} chooses the move and climbs down cleanly.
Name only the loose stone
You stay ready without intervening. {{npc_childhood_younger}} backs up alone to the previous foothold.
Wait for their signal
Months later, {{npc_childhood_younger}} crosses a low wall using the tests they learned. A stone rolls underfoot; they catch themselves and call, “Don’t move yet.”
“I Can Try It Alone”
You choose one simple word. Until it is spoken, {{npc_childhood_younger}} keeps the initiative.
Agree on a help signal
You move in anyway. {{npc_childhood_younger}} climbs down the other side and avoids your hand.
Say you know better
You step back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} climbs down slowly and only thanks you once on the ground.
Step back without comment
{{npc_childhood_younger}} finds you on an outside stair and tests each step before descending. A board cracks; when you move forward, they raise a hand: “Stop deciding for me.”
“Stop Deciding for Me”
Your reply turns supervision into a conversation.
Ask what they want to learn next
You send back one short sentence with no new rule.
Write back “I trust you”
The note comes back covered by one word: “I know.”
Add a list of dangers
A folded note reaches you: {{npc_childhood_younger}} drew a broken plank and wrote, “I know how to test before climbing. You can stop watching every step.”
The Folded Note Under the Door
You shift the discussion from permission to the limit they had set for themselves.
Ask what limit would have made them turn back
You answer that the risk was not foolish because they had planned an exit.
Support the planned risk
Your answer still sounds like an order. {{npc_childhood_younger}} only promises to “think about it.”
Tell them never to do it again
A messenger brings a letter from {{npc_childhood_younger}}. They accepted a medicine delivery through a damaged route after planning a detour. “Would you have let me go?”
The Crossing They Chose
{{npc_childhood_younger}} replies that taking the mockery was harder than walking farther.
Ask what cost the most
You value the moment they gave up on “finishing fast.”
Praise the turn-back, not the delivery
Your reply reduces their decision to something obvious; the next letter will be shorter.
Say it was obvious
The next letter is rain-stained. {{npc_childhood_younger}} abandoned the main route at the first planned warning sign and used the detour, arriving later with the medicine intact.
The Detour Used
{{npc_childhood_younger}} describes the concrete warning sign that changed their mind.
Ask what triggered the turn-back
You write that going and returning were two decisions, not a win followed by a failure.
Recognize both decisions
The next reply begins: “That is not why I turned back.”
Write “I told you so”
{{npc_childhood_younger}} writes that they took another risky task without telling you. This time they turned back halfway: “I decided to go myself, then decided to come back myself.”
The Decision Without Permission
The traveler smiles: “I think they would tell you it is not.”
Send “that is my method”
The traveler carries a message that claims no credit.
Send word that the method is theirs now
You restate one useful limit without asking them to copy your teaching style.
Add a warning never to push the younger kids
A traveler who knows {{npc_childhood_younger}} says they now teach two younger children to test ropes and footholds. “They say you mostly taught them not to trust a support on sight.”
News Through a Traveler
You encourage review without deciding for them whether the act was heroic or foolish.
Ask what they would review afterward
You answer that no rule replaces what they saw on the spot.
Back their judgment in the moment
You prioritize their safety. {{npc_childhood_younger}} replies, “All right. But what if someone truly has no time?”
Advise them to stay out next time
Another letter arrives. {{npc_childhood_younger}} pulled a worker out of a falling load’s path, then wondered whether they risked too much for someone who might have escaped alone.
The Question About Rescue
The reply is late: {{npc_childhood_younger}} dislikes turning every rescue into an automatic excuse.
Say the rescue justifies everything
{{npc_childhood_younger}} decides to face the supervisor instead of hiding the lost tool.
Advise owning the damage
You write that saving someone does not erase the cost, and the cost does not erase the rescue.
Separate the rescue from the loss
Later, {{npc_childhood_younger}} writes that they helped during another accident. The person got out, but a tool was lost and a supervisor blames them for worsening the mess despite the rescue.
Taking the Risk Again
You do not turn the episode into proof that your advice was right.
Admit there was no clean choice
The discussion looks for a concrete threshold instead of general guilt.
Ask what sign would have justified stepping in
{{npc_childhood_younger}} replies, “Then you wanted me to obey, not judge.”
Defend your advice no matter what
{{npc_childhood_younger}} follows your advice during a minor accident and stays back. Nobody is badly hurt, but someone falls while evacuating and later blames them for watching without acting.
The Time They Do Not Step In
event.ch_v2_combat_risk_01_younger_lt_s1: You acknowledge that courage can leave a concrete debt.
Accept that accounting
{{npc_childhood_younger}} describes a safer plan without promising to remain a bystander.
Ask what they would change next time
The line annoys them: “The people who pay afterward are not scenery.”
Say heroes break things
{{npc_childhood_younger}} repaid the lost tool through weeks of work. In the letter, they do not regret the rescue but reject the idea that good intentions erase damage.
The Cost of Acting
You answer that this tension will probably never disappear completely.
Name the problem without solving it
{{npc_childhood_younger}} replies that the phrase is no longer enough to decide for an adult.
Repeat “your safety first”
You explicitly give up on providing a universal rule.
Say the next choice is theirs
{{npc_childhood_younger}} writes that the accusation from the accident still sticks. They want neither to run toward every danger nor use caution to avoid all responsibility.
The Cost of Standing Back
You answer without defending yourself. The disagreement finally becomes something you can name together.
Admit that they are right
The next reply is one line: “Then you were never really listening.”
Say you were always right
You do not use fear as an order; you present it as your part of the problem.
Explain that the fear remains
A longer letter begins: “You taught me to look before acting. But sometimes you still confuse protecting someone with deciding for them.” {{npc_childhood_younger}} asks whether you see it too.
The Words Afterward
The question opens a practical discussion instead of an order to be careful.
Ask for their fallback plan
You refuse to act as final authority. {{npc_childhood_younger}} answers with their own argument, not a request for approval.
Say their judgment is enough to decide
You answer as an equal: one precise concern, without taking over the whole decision.
Point out one concrete weak spot
Years later, {{npc_childhood_younger}} says they will lead a team on dangerous work. Before starting, they send you the plan and add: “I want your opinion, not your permission.”
The Same Warning, Years Later
You answer that the advice had to survive reality, not the other way around.
Approve the change
{{npc_childhood_younger}} details what was protected and what had to be sacrificed.
Ask what their version saved
The reply comes back blunt: “You were not there.”
Defend your original plan
{{npc_childhood_younger}} sends the plan back after the job. They used your advice, but changed it on site when an unexpected constraint appeared. “Useful. Not sacred.”
The Advice, Modified
The reply talks about signs, people, and limits, not what you would have done.
Ask how they decided
You measure their choice against your own again. The reply arrives polite but distant.
Explain what you would have done
For once, no advice follows. {{npc_childhood_younger}} understands the silence.
Simply write “good”
After the job, {{npc_childhood_younger}} writes that the plan changed three times and they had to contradict someone more experienced. “I thought of our old planks, then decided for myself.”
Their Own Judgment
You accept the reversal without joking. The relationship is no longer organized around who protects whom.
Answer as an equal
{{npc_childhood_younger}} answers warmly but does not yield: “Smaller, maybe. Not less capable.”
Say they will always be “the little one”
For the first time, you write with a real question whose answer you have not already chosen.
Send one of your own doubts
The last letter begins with a drawing of the old broken plank. {{npc_childhood_younger}} writes: “I do not ask you to save me anymore. If you ever hesitate before a risk, you can ask me too.”
Equal Before the Risk

item.civilian_workshop_toolkit.descripti: Portable family tools that turn workshop habits into practical repairs on the road.
item.civilian_trust_ledger.description: A neighborhood credit ledger proving trust earned through specific acts, not inherited status.
item.civilian_workshop_cat.description: The workshop cat that learned every adapted route and refuses to stay behind.
item.family_marine_field_compass.descrip: A field compass for choosing a route after reading the terms yourself.
item.family_marine_service_journal.descr: A service journal carried as evidence of duty, doubt, and private memory.
item.marine_courtyard_hound.description: A courtyard hound that follows the family name after the institution gives its symbols back.
item.family_pirate_salt_chart.descriptio: A salt-stained chart whose crossed ports teach caution as much as direction.
item.family_pirate_black_flag_patch.desc: A burned flag patch kept as a rule to test, not a virtue to assume.
item.pirate_safe_harbor_gull.description: A banded harbor gull that remembers refuge signs and unsettled routes.
item.revolutionary_handoff_notebook.desc: A closed handoff notebook that makes invitation and inheritance separate things.
item.revolutionary_boundary_keys.descrip: Two keys carried together so safehouse access and family space stay distinct.
item.revolutionary_courier_ferret.descri: A small courier animal kept as proof that missions must be chosen, not assigned by age.
item.family_royal_plain_seal.description: A plain seal used as proof of history without promising rank or rule.
Unmarked boots for leaving palace routes without denying where you came from.
item.royal_palace_hound.description: A palace hound loyal to the family bond rather than the council obligation.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_lost_button: On a gallery floor, a neighbor searches for a small button engraved with a star. He checks his pockets for the third time and shows you where it rolled under the boards.
Ask him to describe the engraved star
Retrace the neighbor’s path step by step
Search for the button along the baseboards
The star button glints under a low board, too far for your fingers. A string, a twig, and a bit of wax lie nearby.
Show the neighbor where the button is stuck
The neighbor rubs the recovered button on his sleeve and finds the engraved star again. His relief seems huge for something so small.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_spilled_buc: In a narrow passage, your foot knocks over a neighbor’s bucket. Water runs toward everyone’s shoes, and the owner has just turned the corner.
The owner returns to the passage and finds her bucket lying against the wall. She looks at the puddle, then at you, then at the soaked rag without asking a question.
Stand the bucket up and show the puddle
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_blurred_tall: You restore the ledger lines and find the isolated crate behind a neighboring stack.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_closing_bell: Your voice reaches both groups and clearly replaces the silent closing bell.
After the confused bell strikes, one group claims it finished before the other. The local supervisor asks which time counts, and no one has a reliable watch.
You explain that your delay at the bell blurred the stopping time, not the work of either group.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_market_price: You protect the delivery by adding your own money and keeping the shopping list intact.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_missing_toke: At an artisan’s shop, the token proving your purchase drops into a pile of wood shavings. The person who sent you will return soon; without that token, you can prove neither the payment nor the deposit money left behind.
You stop searching and prepare an explanation about the lost token before the supervisor returns.
Turn over the shavings all at once
Sort the shavings around where it fell
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_promised_shi: Leave the post for the paid errand
You keep the promise at the post first, then ask whether the paid errand can still leave with you.
You stay at the post until closing, and the paid errand leaves without you.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_queue_stewar: Refuse the secret deal for tomorrow
The supervisor returns with the final total: one lot is missing compared with the valid tickets. Your earlier choice now has a simple consequence: someone will leave empty-handed.
Serve the adult from the secret deal
You honor the promise made in a whisper and accept that the line will not understand why this customer moves ahead.
You follow the ticket order everyone could verify, even if the last customer without a lot is furious.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_sealed_envel: A clear contradiction appears: he knows the recipient, but not the delivery time requested by the neighbor.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_friend_rule_intro.t: In the yard, a boy your age draws two signs on a board: clap at the first, freeze at the second. He hands you the chalk to invent the third gesture.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_game_spreads.title: Your Rule Has Traveled
event.ch_v2_peers_01_game_spreads.text: In the same yard, younger children are playing the game you invented with your friend. They replaced your third gesture and claim this version has always existed.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_missing_score_token: During a tabletop game, the score token disappears. Two children are already accusing each other; one asks you to decide before everyone starts searching everyone else’s pockets.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_pretend_ship_captai: Your route turns the whole yard into an imaginary archipelago; even your opponents want to follow this course.
Someone throws a large cloth over the crates and announces a storm. The painted rudder is no longer enough: the crew must decide what to do when the planned route collapses.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_younger_lookouts.ch: You confuse the lookouts’ code enough to slow the prank, not enough to protect everyone.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_younger_lookouts_i0: When the prank is about to start, two codes circulate for the lookouts. The younger children stare at each other; the older ones realize their prank no longer belongs entirely to them.
When the lookouts’ code becomes uncertain, you suggest stopping the prank. Some complain, but no one has paid the price of the plan yet.
You deliberately trigger the false start. The prank falls flat, and the older children immediately look for someone to blame.
You show the younger children exactly when to leave. The prank continues, but they are no longer silent pieces.
The prank stops before it really starts. The older children surround the lookouts and ask who changed the codes. The younger children wait for your answer.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_borrowed_br: In a back room, a large broom waits against the wall while an adult tidies farther away. You want to sweep the dust under the shelf, but the handle rises almost over your head.
Study the hand position before sweeping
You copy the essential parts of the sweep: low hands, small motion, pause at the edge. The broom feels almost your size.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_lost_button: Retracing his steps, you spot a round mark that left the path. The button must have continued under a board.
Your foot stops just before crushing a tiny engraved disk. The button is there, caught beside a board.
Ask why the button matters so much
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_lt03a_word_: The merchant has not forgotten the key that stayed in your fist. This time, he leaves you watching a personal bag while he speaks outside, without saying what to do if someone approaches.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_lt04b_awkwa: As you near fifteen, the merchant gives you a tiny mission: guard his stool and coat while he crosses the street. He returns before you have time to forget.
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_lt07b_verif: Keep this verification for future messages
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_rattling_ti: A small closed tin rolls under a chair when your foot touches it. A hard object clicks inside, and an adult had specifically asked you not to disturb this corner.
Listen to the clicking without opening the tin
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_slipping_kn: Point out the object that left the package
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_tiny_delive: When you return, the merchant has already learned that the package arrived. He sets both hands on the counter and only asks whether you would also tell him when a delivery goes wrong.
Promise to report every delivery incident
Promise only to report the result
event.ch_v2_generic_early_01_unclaimed_h: A hat falls from a small cart that just passed and lands in the middle of the path. Three people walk behind it, but none seems to notice the hat is missing.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_after_hours_: After helping repair a mechanism, you forced one piece until it broke. The workshop has just closed and the supervisor will return for his keys soon; the tools and broken piece are still in front of you.
The supervisor operates the mechanism once empty, then under its normal load. The repair holds for now, but he asks what you will do if it breaks tomorrow.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_apprenticesh: Prepare each motion for the order
You organize the whole order around a misread measurement and ruin the first piece.
Your preparation holds until one rushed step; the first piece fails inspection.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_closing_bell: Call the stop to both groups
You catch the rope as you arrive and trigger two confused strikes instead of the planned closing rhythm.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_favor_s02b_s: Someone returns with exactly the agreed sum for an old service and asks whether the money debt is now closed. The payment settles the Berrys, not necessarily what you expect from people.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_favor_s05b_o: The “small favor” eats the planned half-day, then a new request appears because you are already there. The time you refused to count is now costing a real opportunity.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_favor_s10_wh: Refuse without breaking the chain of help
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_market_price: You were given a shopping list and just enough money. At the counter, the total exceeds the handed-over sum; the seller waits while the goods remain separated in front of you.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_mislabeled_c: Trace the order of the two deliveries
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_missing_toke: You narrow the fall zone, but two round tokens appear instead of one certain answer.
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_queue_stewar: Apply the same criterion to both tickets
You change criteria mid-sentence, and the line understands that pressure may be enough to make you yield.
You make the criterion clear for the whole line; no one can later pretend it targeted only those two people.
Write the ticket criterion in front of everyone
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_quiet_counte: You refuse the exchange without humiliating the customer; even the line behind him understands what the merchant allowed you to decide.
You read the wrong ledger line and announce an instruction that does not apply to this customer.
You find the counter instruction and the old transaction that explains why the customer insists today.
The merchant returns and looks at the moved package, the till, and the customer’s face. “So?” He waits for your account of the five minutes before touching anything.
Tell the five minutes in order
event.ch_v2_generic_late_01_sealed_envel: Ask for recipient, seal, and time details
He approves the time you just invented and reveals that he is bluffing.
He repeats your false time word for word, convinced it came from the real sender.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_blocked_passage.cho: You make them believe they will have to explain the blockade to many more children.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_blocked_passage_i01: The adolescents change the blockade: the shortcut is now “members only,” and a marked piece of wood serves as an entry token. The younger children watch your choice.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_entrusted_tool_loan: An adult left you a simple tool to finish repairing a crate. Your friend arrives breathless: he needs it for five minutes and promises no one will know he borrowed it.
Repair the crate with your friend
event.ch_v2_peers_01_friend_rule_intro_i: Your friend performs your third gesture too quickly and trips over his own feet. Two other children stop, intrigued, and want to try your game.
Keep one gesture private between you two
event.ch_v2_peers_01_friend_rumor_exclus: When you ask for details, the rumor changes: the place, the forbidden gesture, and even the game are different depending on who speaks. Your friend still admits one small real fault.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_humiliating_initiat: You make the group laugh without humiliating yourself and force the leader to face his own tradition.
The tradition changes immediately: no one can demand a humiliation they would refuse themselves.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_lt_rival_s05_ask_fo: She Asks for Help She Cannot Win
event.ch_v2_peers_01_lt_rival_s11b_long_: A message arrives very late. She lost a trial you would probably have won, but succeeded at a challenge you have never attempted.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_missing_score_token: Your bluff makes everyone speak in the wrong order and immediately exposes the child who started the accusation.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_pane_reconciliation: Propose a new promise between you
event.ch_v2_peers_01_paper_boat_race.cho: Your fold cuts the current and puts your boat back in the race.
You clear two obstacles in one motion, and the whole paper fleet speeds up.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_pretend_ship_captai: Your course works, but it does not impress enough people to settle the two camps.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_private_rule_repeat: The Sign That Was Only Yours
To make the group laugh, your friend repeats the private sign born from your first game. He smiles for a second, then sees your face and realizes he shared that sign without asking.
Turn the private sign into a public gesture
event.ch_v2_peers_01_rival_praise_revers: Beat her at the next job
You turn the compliment into a clear rivalry rule: the winner always chooses the next measure.
event.ch_v2_peers_01_younger_lookouts.ch: You get a discussion, but no one wants to give up the fun part of the prank.
Your false code goes out at the wrong time, and the younger children become the first accused.
You create a code that lets the younger children withdraw before the older ones begin.
Your new code gives the lookouts control over the start; no one can launch the prank without their agreement.
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_child_size_har: The new routing gains length but jams one buckle. You still need to rethink the strap path.
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_lt01_old_sampl: Show where the “three hands” measure came from
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_lt02_first_sta: Two years later, you are shown two ways to pass on the old measure: a rigid gauge that is easy to copy, or the phrase “three human hands,” faster but less precise.
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_lt13_common_me: Years after the three hands of rope, you receive a method that works without knowing your body or your name. It still keeps one reflex from childhood: verify before calling a measure “standard.”
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_standard_toolb: In the workshop, the supervisor gives you the box with human-sized handles and assigns other posts by build. Daro, a young Giant, refuses only heavy loads; Sumi, a Mink, asks for a tool too.
You separate work from body size, then assign tools by what each person can actually use. The group resumes without imposed posts.
The rotation begins, then two posts need the same key. Sumi keeps the tool and offers to finish her assembly; Daro asks to change the sequence instead of sending them back to old roles.
event.ch_v2_race_human_01_two_hand_instr: You identify the only two useful constraints and can cross out the rest of the drawing without losing the assembly sequence.
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_called_again: Under the pontoon, a mooring line gets stuck during your meal. Three adults are already calling you: “You can go down.” No one has reached for the boathook leaning against the quay.
One short phrase is enough: slack in the line, boathook ready, no one pulls. The mooring line comes back without making your body the only tool.
The rope comes out, but the boat struck a post and your meal cools on the quay. An adult already asks you to dive again and check another line.
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_lt_s08a_term: A passing sailor has heard the story: according to him, you always ask for payment before helping. The rumor kept the price and forgot your choice.
Let the payment speak for itself
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_lt_s11b_refu: Make them repeat that they are really asking
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_net_under_pi: You immediately read the loop sequence and have them slacken exactly the line trapping the net.
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_not_first_to: You cut through the shouting with one clear phrase: rope to the child, ladder clear, no one pulls you out of the water.
Give the child one short phrase
Explain who was at risk of sinking
event.ch_v2_race_fishman_01_price_from_b: The package comes up, but several hooks are bent. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} counts them again in front of you and repeats that, for a Fish-Man, it should have been easy.
Say the next dive will have to be requested
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_drowned_instruc: In a busy room, three adults speak almost at the same time. With your Mink ears, you hear every sentence, but the voices overlap until you no longer know which request was meant for you.
Isolate the voice turned toward you
Ask for one clear request again
Set down your object and ask for turns speaking
You think you finally isolated the right sentence, then its speaker corrects you: part of it was for someone behind you. Hearing every word was not enough to know which action was yours.
Ask them to say your name before the request
The room calms enough to resume. The three adults now wait for your way of sorting voices before restarting the work.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_listen_for_sign: Near the quay, you are asked to listen for the call that announces a boat’s departure. Crates creak, gulls cry, and another very similar call sounds almost at the same moment.
The two calls overlap: one comes from the boat quay, the other from the crate hall. The adults already look at you as if your ears should decide alone.
You finally identify the call from the boat quay. Before everyone resumes, someone asks how to avoid relying entirely on your ears next time.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt01_first_filt: Months later, you are again asked to “listen carefully.” This time, three people agree to specify who is speaking, to whom, and for what action before starting.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt08_layers.tex: A complex request arrives with three useful details and two noisy distractions. You now know to ask for the name, the action, and the deadline before sorting the rest.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt10a_familiar_: A familiar voice calls you from far away, but the quay noise distorts the words. You recognize the person, not yet the requested action.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_lt10b_source_be: A clear call crosses the street, but first you look for who made it and where they are looking. This time, clarity begins before your ears.
event.ch_v2_race_mink_01_trail_after_rai: Under the awning, tracks cross with drops falling from the roof. One fresh print leads toward the storage room, but a soap smell pulls toward the yard.
event.ch_v2_race_giant_01_borrowed_autho: In the yard, an adult asks you to hold the heavy door while he looks for a wedge. Because you are a Giant, two children immediately treat your gestures like orders and line up behind you.
In a small room, the floorboards creak under your young Giant weight. The exit is behind three children sitting on the floor; if you move without warning, everyone will have to shift too fast.
In the square, your Giant shadow covers the screen where an adult is showing gestures to copy. The smaller children can no longer see his hands, and no one dares ask you to move.
event.ch_v2_identity_world_01_departure_: On the quay, a local crew prepares to leave. Everyone gets a task except you; when a crate remains in the middle of the passage, no one knows whether you should take it.
event.ch_v2_identity_world_01_pirate_son: The Song and the Unpaid Tab
The song continues outside, but the innkeeper keeps the bill on the counter. He asks whether your help was about the music, the pirates, or the Berrys owed.
event.ch_v2_identity_world_01_public_cha: Rain starts again on the public chart. Fresh ink runs toward the old route lines, and two travelers are already waiting to copy what you write.
event.ch_v2_identity_world_01_traveling_: On an inn table, a travel notebook passes from hand to hand. One page asks children to add a place they truly know, not a copied rumor.
The notebook returns with a question under your line: should it include what you saw yourself, what a reliable adult says, or what the whole port repeats?
event.ch_v2_origin_cross_civilian_01_min: In a civilian shop, your Mink ears catch rope fibers rubbing under the stairs before the step cracks. The seller keeps serving the line anyway.
event.ch_v2_origin_cross_pirate_01_human: On the quay, a stranger hands you a note marked with a familiar pirate sign and claims to carry a message from your family. He knows your name, but not the agreed word.
event.ch_v2_origin_cross_pirate_01_mink_: The Missing Share at the Counter
In a tavern, your Mink ears hear two pirates recounting shares of loot. One share is missing at the counter, and one of them is already blaming the server.
event.ch_v2_origin_cross_revolutionary_0: The message is almost saved, but the cistern still leaks. The adult asks whether you want to carry the wet letter yourself or stay to fix the leak.
event.ch_v2_origin_cross_royal_01_human_: In a royal archive room, you are handed an unstamped page to file with the ordinary registers. Your human appearance triggers no check, but the paper looks too recent.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_north_blue_01_swa: You give the entry cue too early; the boat has to pull back out and attempt the approach again.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_can: The medical platform is reached. Before the transfer, the caregiver asks whether the splint hit a post or branch during the passage; his check will start there.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_cen: Plot the mast’s route through the wide streets
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_kar: Call an emergency halt to the line
event.ch_v2_birthplace_south_blue_01_sor: Point out the spare boards for the trunk
A second courier bursts into the port crossroads: both recipients have changed handoff points, one higher on the inland road, the other on another pontoon.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_auro: As the cradle is being aligned, a worker recounts the wedges: one is missing. The hull will not move until it is found, and the passage stays closed.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_masa: At Masala Port, performers play at the quay edge while a small ship boards passengers. The crowd steps back with each act and closes the gangway access; you are given the boundary ribbon.
event.ch_v2_birthplace_west_blue_01_sank: The steps are clear. The pilot wants to leave without being caught by the same current again; he asks you to signal when the bow finally points toward the channel.
event.family_civilian_01_fathers_work_be: Your father is still holding your spoon when the bell of his small shop rings. A customer waits behind the half-open shutter; the meal cools while he hesitates between you and the counter.
You clutch the spoon against your bowl. Your father sees the meal is not over before lifting the shutter.
You reach for him. He answers the customer without letting go of your bowl and slows down.
You pat the counter. The customer leans toward you and your father has to serve without simply moving you aside.
Your father opens the shutter with one hand and keeps hold of your bowl with the other. The customer sets a coin on the counter and asks to be served quickly.
You take the customer's coin and hold it out to your father. He laughs, takes it, and finishes the sale one-handed.
Pull his sleeve toward the bowl
You tug his sleeve toward your bowl. Your father asks the customer to wait a minute and takes the spoon again.
You push the coin toward the edge. Your father catches it and realizes you do not want to play shop now.
event.family_civilian_01_two_parents_ren: Your mother slips a rent receipt under a bowl to keep it from blowing away. Your father wants to pay today; she wants to keep enough Berrys to replace a cracked cooking pot.
You grab the large coin in the middle of the table. Your parents stop arguing to keep it from falling.
You pat the cracked pot with your palm. Your mother steadies it; your father immediately looks at the receipt under the bowl.
You slide the receipt out from under the bowl. Your father takes it back while your mother brings the pot beside the coins.
Your father lines up the coins beside the receipt. Your mother sets the cracked pot next to it: paying one now means making the other wait.
Give the coin to your father
You place the coin in your father's hand. He keeps it by the receipt while your mother points out the pot still has to last.
Drop the coin into the pot
You drop the coin into the pot. Your mother smiles despite herself; your father retrieves it without hiding that he disagrees.
Keep the coin in your fist
You refuse to open your hand. Your parents have to stop treating you like a tie-breaker and make the decision themselves.
event.family_civilian_01_orphan_supper_k: After supper, a neighbor sets a key on the table and reminds the baker he is only housing you until tomorrow. No adult wants you outside; none can keep you without a cost.
You close your fingers around the key. The neighbor stops talking long enough to make sure you do not put it in your mouth.
Offer the key to the neighbor
You offer the key to the neighbor. She does not take it right away and looks to the baker to see who will open the next door.
You leave the table and crawl toward the baker. He holds you against his leg while the neighbor folds your blanket.
The baker counts the occupied beds while the neighbor folds your blanket. They discuss your next roof like a delivery that still needs an address.
Give the key to the baker
You place the key in the baker's hand. He sighs, then says he will keep you tonight and look for another door tomorrow.
Offer the blanket to the neighbor
You pull the blanket toward the neighbor. She takes it with you still wrapped in it and makes the adults deal with tonight before tomorrow.
Hide the key under the blanket
You tuck the key under your blanket and refuse to give it back. The adults realize their back-and-forth already costs you something.
event.family_civilian_01_poor_patched_ro: A short rain comes through the patched roof and fills a bucket beside your bed. Your father moves the flour sacks while the landlord is already asking for rent at the door.
Push the bucket under the leak
You push the bucket toward the drip with your foot. Your father rights it without taking his eyes off the landlord.
You grab a flour sack and tug it away from the water. Your father comes to help you, leaving the landlord waiting in the doorway.
You cry when the landlord raises his voice. Your father picks you up with one arm and the argument changes tone immediately.
The landlord points to the date in his notebook. Inside, the bucket is nearly overflowing and the flour must stay dry until the morning market.
You hold the small dry sack against you while your father moves the rest. The landlord has to wait until the flour is safe.
You bang the rim when the water rises. Your father leaves the landlord's notebook alone and empties the bucket first.
You reach until your father picks you up. The landlord keeps his notebook open, but the negotiation waits behind your immediate need.
event.family_civilian_01_wealthy_shop_ke: Before opening, an employee brings the keyring to the adults running the family business. Three doors lead to three full storerooms; they are already arguing about which one should be expanded this year.
You shake the keyring until every key jingles. The adults stop comparing papers and look at which one you grabbed.
Give a key to your mother
You nearly pull off a small key and offer it to your mother. Your father notices before the employee takes the ring back.
You drop the keyring on the floor. The employee crouches to pick it up, interrupting the expansion argument.
The employee keeps the keyring extended while the adults compare sales, wages, and repairs. Everyone is waiting to know which storeroom opens first.
Offer the large key to your father
You choose the largest key and offer it to your father. He takes it as a game, not as your opinion on the business.
Offer a key to the employee
You offer a key to the employee still waiting on his feet. Your mother laughs and finally asks which storeroom actually makes his work harder.
You press the keyring to your belly. The adults have to come to you and the business argument loses its urgency for a few seconds.
event.family_civilian_01_giant_narrow_co: In the small family shop, your Giant knee already knocks beneath a counter built for humans. Your father wedges a board under the table while a customer waits for an order.
Nudge the stool with your knee
Your knee nudges the stool into the counter. Your father immediately sees the added board still leaves too little room.
You pat the board your father just wedged in. It shakes enough to make the customer's basket move back.
You reach over the too-low counter. Your father stops before you can knock over the waiting order.
The counter tilts as soon as your father adds the board. The customer pulls back his basket: either the order is served now or the furniture is taken apart in front of him.
Hold the board with your foot
You pin the board with one foot while your father serves the customer. It holds just long enough to finish the order.
You pull your knee away and refuse to stay wedged under the counter. Your father moves the order instead of forcing you into the space.
You shove the stool away from the counter. Your father understands the patch is not enough and serves the customer standing with you beside him.
event.family_civilian_01_fishman_washbas: A customer pushes the washbasin away after seeing your Fish-Man hands in it. Your mother is still holding his change; he demands another basin before accepting his order.
Pull your hands from the water
You pull your hands out and splash the rim. The customer steps back again; your mother puts down her coins to look at you.
You push the basin away from the customer. It slides to your mother, who understands exactly what you are reacting to.
You cling to your mother's leg. She steps between you and the customer before answering his demand.
The customer keeps his parcel closed and points at the basin as if it spoiled the whole order. Your mother looks at you before answering his demand.
You put your hands back in the same basin. Your mother serves the customer with that water and refuses to replace it for his comfort.
You stay against her without touching the parcel. Your mother finishes the sale at her pace and keeps the customer at a distance.
You push the sealed parcel back toward the customer. Your mother catches it before it falls and tells him he can shop elsewhere.
event.family_civilian_01_household_fallb: In the morning, the household shutter refuses to rise and blocks the only window to the street. A neighbor brings a hammer; the first delivery of the day is already waiting at the door.
You grab the hammer handle left too close to you. The neighbor gently takes it back and moves it from the edge.
You slap the shutter with your palm. It barely moves, enough to make the waiting courier laugh.
Push the parcel toward the window
You push the parcel on the floor toward the light. The courier catches it and shows the neighbor the entrance is still blocked.
The neighbor slips the hammer under the hinge while the courier sets the parcel down. Every strike risks breaking the wood even further.
You hold the small wedge the neighbor gives you while he lifts the hinge. He takes it back before the next strike.
Drag the parcel from the hammer
You drag the parcel away from where the hammer is falling. The adults finally clear a safe space around you.
Drop the wedge and back away
You drop the wedge and back away into the room. The neighbor stops involving you and finishes the repair with the courier.
event.family_civilian_02_father_customer: At four, you recognize the regulars before your father does. He searches his order book while a customer insists she already paid for the repair sitting on the counter.
You point at the stain before your father turns the page. The customer seizes on it and insists that is exactly where he wrote down her payment.
You repeat that the customer 'already paid.' Your father closes the book for a second and asks when she remembers coming.
You pull the repaired item toward you instead of handing it over. Your father and the customer have to finish their argument before it leaves the counter.
Your father turns two pages and stops: no payment is recorded. The customer points to an ink stain she says she saw on the day she left the item.
Look for a mark on the page
You trace the lines with your finger and find a mark your father forgot. He checks it himself before returning the item to the customer.
You push the book toward your father and refuse to decide. He checks every page again while the customer waits for his answer.
Put the item back on the counter
You put the repair back out of the customer's reach. Your father handles the dispute himself and asks you to leave the book alone.
event.family_civilian_02_parents_expense: Your parents place the last large coin of the week between a prescription and a coal bill. Your father wants the medicine; your mother argues that without heat no one will work tomorrow.
Put the coin on the prescription
You put the large coin on the doctor's note. Your father nods; your mother immediately points to the nearly cold hearth.
Put the coin on the coal sack
You move the coin toward the empty coal sack. Your mother pins it with a finger and your father reminds her the medicine cannot wait long.
Hide the coin under your bowl
You hide the coin under your bowl. Your parents stop looking at you as a tie-breaker and resume the disagreement themselves.
The apothecary waits at the door and the coal seller holds his cart in the street. Your parents refuse to pretend both costs can be covered.
You run to the door and wave the apothecary inside. He agrees to prepare only what is needed while your parents keep enough for some coal.
Pull the blanket toward the sick person
You pull the blanket toward the sick person and look at the dead fire. Your parents see both needs are real and cut each purchase down.
Give the coin back to your mother
You put the coin back in your mother's hand and leave the table. Your parents have to decide without making a four-year-old carry the choice.
event.family_civilian_02_orphan_borrowed: The blanket you have used for months suddenly bears another family’s name in charcoal. The evening guardian says it must be returned before night, even though your next bed has nothing ready.
You wrap yourself in the marked blanket before it is folded. The caretaker has to look at you while explaining why she wants it back.
You point to the black letters on the corner. The caretaker explains they belong to another family returning tonight.
Put your little bag on it
You put your small bag on the blanket as if to claim it. The caretaker stops before pulling it out from under the bag.
The guardian folds the blanket over her arms. Your small bag still has room, but nothing warm enough for the night ahead.
Carry the blanket to the door
You carry the folded blanket to the door. The caretaker promises another layer for tonight instead of pretending the cold is not a problem.
Keep one corner of the blanket
You refuse to let go of one corner. The caretaker cuts an old lining for your bag before returning the rest to the other family.
You sit on it and refuse to move. The adults have to find a concrete replacement before they can take it back.
event.family_civilian_02_poor_credit_cha: The merchant adds another chalk mark to your household account before handing over the rice sack. The old slate is almost full; he warns he will add nothing more after today.
You count the large visible chalk marks with your finger. The merchant corrects you, then shows your father the board is nearly full.
You point to the sack behind his foot. The merchant pulls it closer but keeps a hand on it until an adult answers.
Hide the chalk in your palm
You close your hand around the chalk. The merchant asks for it back and your father steps in before the game turns into a new promise.
The merchant holds the chalk between two fingers and shows you the slate. The rice sack stays behind his foot until someone accepts the new debt.
You rub at an old mark your father says was already paid. The merchant checks, erases it himself, and frees a little space on the board.
You take the smaller rice sack the merchant agrees to release today. The household leaves with less rice, but without adding a full new line of debt.
You put the chalk back in his hand and step away from the counter. Your father has to negotiate without treating your gesture as consent.
event.family_civilian_02_wealthy_wage_en: An employee brings the wage envelopes while a foreman asks for a new machine. The people running the family business can fund both, but not without delaying the expansion announced for months.
You sort the envelopes like cards without understanding the amounts. An employee notices one is missing and calls the foreman.
Carry an envelope to the employee
You carry the envelope you are shown to its owner. He thanks the child before asking the adults why his pay is late.
You repeat the word the foreman has been saying for five minutes. The adults laugh for a second, then the employee reminds them wages come before projects.
The envelopes remain sealed on the desk. The foreman unrolls the machine quote beside them, close enough to cover one employee’s name.
You carry the sealed envelopes one by one without opening them. The adults have to discuss the machine while the wages actually go to the employees.
Give the quote back to the foreman
You push away the large quote covering the names. The foreman rolls it up and the envelopes become the first thing visible on the desk again.
Leave the office with your toy
You take your toy and leave the office. The adults stop presenting the argument as something you are expected to decide now.
event.family_civilian_02_giant_rebuilt_b: Your father has raised the workbench with beams, but a cart wheel now blocks the customers’ path. The choice is between a workshop where you can help and a shop where others can move.
Squeeze between the bench and wheel
You try to squeeze between the raised bench and the wheel. Your shoulder nudges the furniture before you reach the stool.
Roll the wheel with your foot
You move the wheel with your foot. Your father sees it blocks the passage much more than your stool does.
You point to the two customers waiting in the doorway. Your father stops measuring and finally looks at the aisle the way they do.
A Workshop for More Than One Size
Your father pushes the wheel against the wall and measures the aisle with a rope. Two customers wait outside because they can no longer pass your stool.
You hold one end of the rope while your father shifts the bench. He finds an aisle where your stool and a customer can finally pass each other.
Refuse the corner that traps you
You back away from the corner where your father wants the stool. He gives up that measurement instead of making your body the part that has to adapt.
Push the stool out of the shop
You push your stool all the way outside. Your father sees the new bench is pointless if you have to stay out for customers to pass.
event.family_civilian_02_fishman_slipper: Your mother gives you a crate of sea vegetables too slippery for the counter tongs. Your Fish-Man hands sort them quickly; an impatient customer asks you directly to prepare his order.
You separate the slippery greens into small handfuls. The customer sees you are faster than the tongs and starts dictating his order to you.
Repeat the order to your mother
You repeat every word to your mother instead of serving the customer directly. She keeps the coins and takes over the conversation.
Keep your hands on the crate
You keep both hands on the crate without making his parcel. The customer has to wait for your mother to say what to take.
Your mother pushes the crate toward you and keeps the Berrys. This time the customer lists his order without going through her.
You fill exactly the cone your mother shows you. She takes the payment herself and reminds the customer you are helping her, not working for him.
Route every request through your mother
At every new request, you look to your mother before moving. The customer quickly learns he cannot order you around directly.
You close the lid and keep your hands on it. Your mother takes over the whole order, slower but on her terms.
event.family_civilian_02_family_room_fal: Work has swallowed the family table: screws, bills, and twine occupy the plates’ place. An adult sweeps everything aside with one arm to serve dinner before the next order arrives.
You catch the screw before it falls. The adult shows you the small jar for it while clearing space for a plate.
Slide the invoice from under the plate
You gently pull the invoice from under the plate. The adult takes it and puts it off the table before serving.
Pile the twine in one corner
You push the twine into a pile to make room. The adult realizes dinner will never start if work keeps the whole table.
Push the tools back like your father did
You push the tools to the edge first, like during earlier interrupted meals. The adult recognizes the gesture and clears a real place to eat.
Make a Table Inside the Work
A bill remains stuck under a plate and a screw rolls toward the edge. Dinner can begin only if someone restores a little order.
Put the screws in their jar
You put the visible screws in the little jar and stop there. The adult finishes the rest as the plates arrive.
Put your plate in the middle
You put your plate in the only clear space. The adults have to move their invoices if they want to keep talking shop through dinner.
Leave the tools where they are
You sit down without tidying anything else. The adult sighs, packs the tools away, and owns the mess as theirs.
